title: Chapter 1 — Sugar Palace
description: A landlord with a padlock, a girl with one bag, and a hotel that is all you ever built.

cards.title: South Street, Iyana-Wahala
cards.text: Sugar Palace Hotel & Bar. Rooms by the hour. Pepper soup by the bowl. Generator by the grace of God.

cards.title: {name}
cards.text: They call you Mama Sugar. You came from Warri twenty-two years ago with one bag and a cousin's address that was wrong. Everything on this street, you saw built. This one, you built.

cards.title: The month
cards.text: Thirty days. Chief Dapo wants his rent. Commander Bassey wants his settlement. Your daughter Ivie wants to know why her school fees are always paid in cash.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Seven a.m. The bar smells of last night: Star lager, Indomie, perfume that was sold as Chanel. Kokoro the bouncer is asleep on two plastic chairs. There is a letter under the door.

beats.speaker: chiefDapo
beats.text: (The letter, in a hand that has written many letters like it.) "Madam. Arrears: ₦250,000. Pay before the end of the month or I padlock. — Chief Dapo, JP." (Under it, in pencil: "No more pepper soup instead.")

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A girl is standing at the gate with a Ghana-must-go bag and a scrap of paper. Nineteen, maybe. Her shoes are her best shoes. You can tell because they hurt her.

beats.speaker: blessing
beats.text: Good morning ma. Please... my cousin Joy said to come here. She said you help girls. (She holds out the paper.) I want to learn hair. I can do braids, cornrow, Ghana weaving. I can wash plates. Anything, ma.

beats.speaker: kokoro
beats.text: (Waking up.) Mama, Joy left for Golden Fleece last month. Alhaja Rukky pays more. (He looks at the girl.) This one is fresh. Rukky will take her by evening.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The girl is waiting. She has not let go of the bag.

options.text: "You will work the bar. Plates, drinks, money. Nothing upstairs. Ever."
"There is a room upstairs. The girls will show you how it works here."
Give her ₦10,000 for transport. "Go home, my daughter. Lagos is not for you."

beats.speaker: blessing
beats.text: (She looks at the money. Then at you.) Home has nothing, ma. That is why I came. (She takes the money anyway, politely, and walks towards Golden Fleece.)

beats.speaker: blessing
beats.text: (She bursts into tears, then apologises for bursting into tears, then washes every glass in the bar without being asked.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chief Dapo arrives at noon in a white Peugeot 406 that has outlived two of his wives. He does not come in. He never comes in during the day.

beats.speaker: chiefDapo
beats.text: Madam. ₦250,000. I am not a wicked man. I am a man with a mortgage.

beats.speaker: chiefDapo
beats.text: He is holding the padlock already. It is new. He bought it for you.

options.text: "Chief, you come here every Thursday night. Should I tell your wife it is for pepper soup?"
"End of the month, Chief. You will have it. All."

variants.text: (His face goes grey, then purple.) End of the month, Madam. And we will never discuss Thursday.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Four o'clock. The girls come down for their meeting: Kemi, who is saving for nursing school; Precious, who laughs too loud; Tari, who never says where she is from. They split the night's money with you. They have always split it sixty-forty. Your sixty.

beats.speaker: blessing
beats.text: (Quietly, from the bar.) Mama, can I ask? Is it true they keep only forty?

variants.text: (Quietly, from the stairs.) Mama... is it true we keep only forty?
(Kemi, reading your face.) Mama, the rent. Are you going to cut our share again?

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The girls are looking at you. The rent is looking at you too.

options.text: "Seventy-thirty until the rent is paid. We all suffer together."

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The rent is ₦{stat:rentDebt} and the month is short. Everybody works.

beats.objective: Work the bar: SELL DRINKS at Sugar Palace (South Street) and raise ₦50,000 towards the rent.

options.text: Keep it. You will need it for Bassey.

beats.title: Sugar Palace
beats.summary: The rent is a clock, and you can hear it ticking over the generator.
